source_text.body:
Automate browser chores with Comet
Commenters use Comet to refine front-end design, work while they grade projects, and read release emails to add songs to a Spotify playlist.
Done with
PC
Perplexity Comet
What they did
Commenters describe using Comet as a browser agent for small web chores they can hand off mid-task. One had it post deadline-extension announcements and update assignment due dates across three Canvas classes while they graded; another told it to read release emails from a Gmail label and add the new items to an existing Spotify playlist; a designer used screenshots and back-and-forth prompts to get front-end feedback on spacing, fonts, and layout.
How it went
Reported outcomes were mainly time savings and convenience: the music workflow saved one commenter about an hour each week, and the instructor said Comet handled the class updates while they worked on something else. Limits also showed up in the thread, with some users calling tasks unreliable or slow.
Worth knowing
The clearest concrete payoff in the thread was the Gmail-to-Spotify routine saving about an hour per week.
Try it yourself
with
Perplexity Comet
Copy prompt
Open my inbox and find the [newsletter or label, e.g. new music release emails] from the past [week]. Pull out each [song and artist] mentioned and add them to my [Spotify] playlist named [playlist name], skipping duplicates. Finish with a list of what you added and anything you couldn't find, and ask me before you change any other playlist or account setting.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/perplexity_ai/comments/1odzml6/do_you_use_comet_browser_what_tasks_do_you
